claim: Germany and the Soviet Union signed a non-aggression pact on 23 August 1939; the Hiranuma cabinet resigned and General Abe formed a cabinet on 30 August; a ceasefire at Nomonhan was agreed on 15 September
source: Wikipedia, Hiranuma cabinet and Nobuyuki Abe; JACAR chronology (15 September 1939); FRUS 1939 vol. IV
note: The Hiranuma resignation is dated 28 or 30 August by different sources; the report says only that it resigned. One timeline gives 16 September for the ceasefire.

claim: Zhukov attacked in August with tanks and artillery and mauled the Japanese 23rd Division; the staff planned to renew the fighting; Umezu and Sugiyama held the positions given
source: From memory of the standard histories
note: To be checked. The positions of the advisers are interpretation.

claim: France asked for an armistice in June 1940; the Governor-General in Hanoi accepted a Japanese demand to stop shipments to China on 20 June; General Nishihara's mission reached Hanoi at the end of June; Japanese troops crossed the border in September and fought at Lang Son
source: FRUS 1940 vol. IV (telegram of 20 June); Wikipedia, Japanese invasion of French Indochina and Indochina Expeditionary Army
note: The sources differ by a day or two on the ultimatum and the accord (4 or 22 September). The report states the 20 June demand and the end-of-June mission only.

claim: After the spring exercise of 1940 Roosevelt kept the Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor and not San Diego; Richardson objected and made two trips to Washington
source: National WWII Museum, 'Solely a Bluff: Relocating the US Fleet to Pearl Harbor'; Wikipedia, James O. Richardson and United States Pacific Fleet
note: The order is dated May or June 1940 by different sources; the report says May. That Hawaii lacked tenders, tankers and training facilities is Richardson's argument as the sources give it.

claim: Richardson lunched with Roosevelt on 8 October 1940 and objected to the fleet being at Hawaii; a Washington newsletter predicted on 26 October that he would be relieved; Kimmel took the fleet on 1 February 1941
source: Wikipedia, James O. Richardson and Husband E. Kimmel; National WWII Museum
note: One source gives January 1941 for the relief. That Richardson said the Navy's senior officers lacked confidence in the civilian leadership is from the same sources.

claim: In May and June 1941 a carrier (Yorktown), three battleships, four light cruisers and a number of destroyers were moved from the Pacific Fleet to the Atlantic
source: Pacific Fleet history pages; DFAT Documents on Australian Foreign Policy vol. 4 (cables of June 1941)
note: The counts differ between sources (fourteen or nineteen destroyers); the report says a number of destroyers. That the carrier was Yorktown is from memory and unchecked.
